blocks.text: Living in Bridal Falls

parts.t: Bridal Falls is an unincorporated community in the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area D, east of the City of Chilliwack. It is not inside the City, and no official boundary for it was found.

The FVRD’s Electoral Area D Housing Needs Report (March 2021) describes Area D, which includes Popkum and Bridal Falls, as bounded by the Fraser River to the northwest, Electoral Area B to the north and east, Electoral Area E to the south and the City of Chilliwack to the west. It describes Bridal Falls as a highway-services community with several tourist and recreation attractions.

blocks.text: Bridal Falls What people recognise

parts.t: Falls
Bridal Veil Falls, which BC Parks says tumble 60 metres over a smooth rock face. The park became a Provincial Park in 1965
History

In the early 1900s the falls generated electricity for the Bridal Falls Chalet, and traces of the generator foundation remain. The park is at the site of the ancient village of Popkum, with settlement records back to the 1700s

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Bridal Falls

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

Popkum-Bridal Falls (Area D) Official Community Plan, FVRD Bylaw No. 1501: a public hearing was held on December 15, 2020, and the FVRD’s First Quarter Update 2021 says the Board adopted it in January 2021.
Bridal Falls is in an FVRD electoral area, Area D, which the FVRD report places outside the City of Chilliwack. The FVRD, not the City, sets its plan and zoning.
ALR: ALR status is parcel-specific, so check the exact parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission map.

Flood: Published municipal records do not list an FVRD or BC document stating a flood or debris-flow hazard for the Bridal Falls area, so check site-specific hazard mapping with the FVRD before building or buying. At the park itself, BC Parks warns that the base of the falls is extremely hazardous.
Transit: BC Transit says route 71 on-request trips can route to Bridal Falls. No other BC Transit route serving it.
Bridal Falls is outside the City of Chilliwack, so City zoning does not apply. The FVRD sets zoning for Electoral Area D. Send me the address and I’ll point you to the right FVRD rules.

blocks.text: Bridal Falls questions

parts.t: Where is Bridal Falls?
Bridal Falls is an unincorporated community in FVRD Electoral Area D, east of the City of Chilliwack. No official boundary for it was found.
Area D is bounded by the Fraser River to the northwest, Electoral Area B to the north and east, Electoral Area E to the south and the City of Chilliwack to the west.
Ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from Bridal Falls?

BC Transit route 71 Agassiz–Harrison runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Harrison Hot Springs, through Rosedale, and its on-request trips can route to Bridal Falls. That means Bridal Falls is served on request, not by a fixed stop on every trip.
No other BC Transit route serving Bridal Falls.
See the
route 71 page
Which school is near Bridal Falls?

Rosedale Traditional Community School (kindergarten to grade 8), at 50850 Yale Rd, is the SD33 school on the Rosedale, Popkum and Bridal Falls side of the district. No school is in Bridal Falls itself.
Use the official SD33 School Locator to confirm the secondary school, so check an exact address with the
SD33 School Locator
What parks and library are near Bridal Falls?
Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park is 16 km east of Chilliwack, off Exit 135, with a loop trail to a viewing platform.
Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (53480 Elgey Road) is a 107-hectare FVRD park with a floating boardwalk and no pets allowed.
There is no library branch in Bridal Falls. The nearest are Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue) and Agassiz Library (7140 Cheam Avenue).
What plan covers Bridal Falls?
The Popkum-Bridal Falls (Area D) Official Community Plan, FVRD Bylaw No. 1501, adopted by the FVRD Board in January 2021.
Is Bridal Falls in a floodplain?

Published municipal records do not list an FVRD or BC document stating a flood or debris-flow hazard for the Bridal Falls area, so check site-specific hazard mapping with the FVRD before building or buying.
At Bridal Veil Falls, BC Parks warns the base of the falls is extremely hazardous, with slippery footing and falling rock and ice.
Ask me or the FVRD about a specific lot.

ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
Agricultural Land Commission map
